title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-7
content:
Quick personal notes + breadcrumbs while debugging seqlen edge-case (KV cache + attention kernel selection).

Summary:
- Intermittent crashes / wrong outputs observed when serving long-context requests (seq_len > 2048) on dedicated A100 nodes.
- Failure surface: tensor shape mismatch / kv_cache index errors after kernel auto-selection switches to flash-attn path.
- Reproducible locally with a short harness (see steps below). Changing attention kernel to memory_efficient avoids the crash.

Environment:
- Model: redwood-verified/opt-6.7b-rlhf-quant (caveat: quant profile applied)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.8.2-rc (branch: kv-cache-fix-tentative)
- GPU: A100-80GB (driver 535, cuda 12.2)
- Config: max_seq_len=4096, kv_cache_sharding=enabled, continuous_batching=true, attention_kernel=auto

Repro steps (local harness):
1) checkout branch: git checkout kv-cache-fix-tentative
2) start local server: ./dev/start_local_runtime.sh --config configs/local-a100.yaml
3) run reproduce script: python tools/repro_long_seq.py \
   --model redwood-verified/opt-6.7b-rlhf-quant \
   --batch 1 --prompt-file tests/long_prompts/prompt_4k.txt \
   --max-seq 4096 --stream=false

Observed failure (server log snippets):
[2025-02-18 14:12:03,422] INFO Selected attention kernel: flash_attention_fwd (heuristic: seq_len>2048 && model.fw_supports_flash)
[2025-02-18 14:12:03,425] ERROR kv_cache: shard_update: index_out_of_range: attempted write at index=4096, capacity=4096
[2025-02-18 14:12:03,426] ERROR runtime: inference failed: KVCacheIndexError: past_kv write out-of-bounds, layer=10, batch_idx=0, write_pos=4096, alloc_len=4096
[2025-02-18 14:12:03,427] ERROR stacktrace: File "/srv/serving/runtime/kv_cache.py", line 312, in write_past_kv
    dst[write_pos:write_pos+chunk_len] = src_chunk
IndexError: slice assignment index out of range

Client-side symptom: truncated generation / repeated tokens then hang (client waits until timeout). Not always crash; sometimes the request completes with garbage tokens.

Commands tried and quick notes:
- Re-run with attention_kernel forced:
  * --attention-kernel=memory_efficient => no crash, latency +5% but stable
  * --attention-kernel=flash_attention => reproduces reliably
- Dumped past_kv shapes right before write: added logging in kv_cache.write_past_kv
  * expected shape: (num_layers=32, heads=32, seq=4096/kv_chunk_size, head_dim=64)
  * actual write_pos occasionally equals alloc_len (4096) which triggers out-of-range when trying to write chunk_len>0
- Tried disabling kv_cache_sharding => crash disappears (indicates bug in shard index math)
- Verified that when continuous_batching=true the failure rate increases (maybe interplay with offset accumulation across batches)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel-specific layout assumption mismatch: flash-attn path expects contiguous past_kv layout (pack/unpack) but our shard update path writes per-chunk with offset computed for memory_efficient layout. Kernel selection switches code paths but not the offsets.
2) Off-by-one/overflow in kv_shard index arithmetic when seq_len % shard_size == 0 (e.g., 4096 % 64 == 0) causing write_pos to equal alloc_len on boundary requests. Happens only when kernel==flash and sharding enabled.
3) Race with continuous batching: offsets are accumulated across micro-batches and we double-apply offset correction for flash path due to different chunk_size semantics.
4) Quantization/compaction path interacting with kernel tile sizes causing slightly different effective seq_len rounding.

Quick local debug artifacts (copied outputs):
-- kv_cache write debug (layer 10) --
pre_write: alloc_len=4096, current_pos=4056, chunk_len=40, computed_write_pos=4096
write attempt -> IndexError

attention kernel selection debug log: 
heuristic: model.fw_supports_flash = True
seq_len=4096 -> selected flash_attention_fwd

Reduced repro to minimal python that reproduces the indexing error (added to tests/regressions):
# minimal repro (tests/regressions/test_kv_shard_index.py)
import numpy as np
from runtime.kv_cache import KVShard
shard = KVShard(num_layers=32, alloc_len=4096, shard_size=64)
# simulate writing sequential chunks
pos = 0
for i in range(64):
    chunk_len = 64
    write_pos = pos + chunk_len
    # bug: on last iteration write_pos == alloc_len -> invalid slice
    shard.write_chunk(layer=10, batch_idx=0, write_pos=write_pos-64, data=np.zeros((chunk_len,)))

What changed recently (suspects):
- Commit: serving-runtime@1.8.2 -> "kv cache shard indexing refactor" (PR #1398) touched write_past_kv and the kernel selection heuristics.
- PR #1404 added flash-attn path integration with slightly different chunking semantics.
- We didn't add cross-tests covering exact boundary conditions (seq_len multiples of shard_size).

Immediate mitigations tested:
- Force attention-kernel=memory_efficient on Dedicated in prod: reduces incidents to zero (degraded perf).
- Disable kv_cache_sharding globally: reduces incidents but increases memory by ~15% (not ideal).
- Add a guard in write_past_kv: if write_pos >= alloc_len: cap at alloc_len-1 and log. (temporary bandaid; hides underlying bug)

Next steps (actionable):
- [ ] Unit test: add regression for seq_len multiples of shard_size (tests/regressions/test_kv_shard_index.py) — I added a draft test that reproduces locally.
- [ ] Add assertions in write_past_kv to fail fast with clearer message including kernel selection and shard metadata.
- [ ] Reproduce with different GPUs (T4) to confirm kernel selection heuristics differ by GPU capability. Samir to run on T4 farm.
- [ ] Revert the index arithmetic change in PR #1398 and re-run the full integration test battery.
- [ ] Add e2e test in CI: run one long-context sample with attention_kernel=auto with sharding enabled and assert no IndexError.
- [ ] Investigate memory layout conversion between flash path and memory_efficient path; add explicit pack/unpack step if needed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is flash-attn implementation requiring a different kv layout (e.g., interleaved heads) compared to our stored past_kv? If so, kernel selection should trigger a conversion step.
- Should we change heuristic to avoid auto-selecting flash for seq_len exact multiples of shard_size until we fix shard math?
- How to quantify perf cost of leaving memory_efficient as default for long-run (for customers on Dedicated)?

Notes for PR message (draft):
- Revert/regress the shard indexing change that introduced boundary off-by-one when seq_len % shard_size == 0.
- Add defensive checks + regression tests.
- Mark as HOTFIX for Dedicated clusters using A100 with sharding enabled.

Slack breadcrumbs:
- initial report: @morgan in #serving-runtime 2025-02-17 09:12 (request id ran-20250217-xx)
- triage + repro: thread with @samir 2025-02-18 11:33
- mitigation: pinned kernel to memory_efficient on prod 2025-02-19 03:20 (ops ticket SERV-2897)

Logs / debug artifacts saved: s3://redwood-internal/debug/kv-cache/2025-02-18/ (server logs, heap snapshots, small reproducer)

Personal notes: this smells like a classic off-by-one around chunk boundaries. Kernel selection makes it visible because flash-attn uses different chunk sizes and will try to write the last chunk aligned to alloc_len. First fix is add tight assertion and better error message. Then either adjust index math or perform layout conversion.

If I get time today: try to patch write_past_kv to compute write_pos = min(write_pos, alloc_len - chunk_len) and add assert that write_pos >= 0. If that fixes tests, open hotfix PR and roll to staging.

-- end of scratchpad --
